title: "If he said it, it is true"
hookLine: Mecca mocks the night journey, and Abu Bakr says, if he said it, it is true (sirah)
carry: he weighed the speaker, not the distance

cards: Morning in Mecca. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells the people what happened in the night: he was carried to Jerusalem and brought back before dawn. In the sirah the reaction is fast.
Some laugh. Ibn Ishaq reports that some who had believed turned back. A caravan takes a month to get there and a month to return, people say, and he did it in one night?
A few of them hurry off to find his close friend, Abu Bakr. Have you heard what your companion is saying now? Today: al-Siddiq.

teach.b: Abu Bakr asks one question first: did he say that? Yes, they say.

teach.h: IF HE SAID IT, IT IS TRUE.
teach.b: In Ibn Ishaq's account he answers: if he said it, then it is true. And he adds, roughly: why are you so surprised?
He tells me news comes to him from heaven, from God, in an hour of the night or the day, and I believe him in that. This is further than Jerusalem.

Then Abu Bakr goes to the Prophet and asks him to describe the city, and as he does, Abu Bakr keeps saying: you have spoken the truth. Tradition says this is the day he was called al-Siddiq, the one who affirms the truth.

Bukhari has a report from the Prophet's side of that morning: when Quraysh would not believe him, Allah showed him Jerusalem, and he described it to them while looking at it. Notice what Abu Bakr's trust rests on.
Not a feeling about miracles, but long knowledge of one man, and of what he has said before. He doesn't weigh the distance to Jerusalem.
And with his answer, this part of the story, sorrow, Ta'if and the night journey, comes to its close.
It began with two graves, Khadijah's and Abu Talib's. It closes with a friend who stays when others mock.

how: Muslims remember Abu Bakr by the title al-Siddiq and retell his answer when they recall the night journey, often on the night of al-Isra wal-Mi'raj.

o: the one who affirms the truth; Abu Bakr's title
a close friend; the word for any loyal companion
one who saw the night journey with his own eyes

p: laughed and ran to Abu Bakr

shown to him as he described it

s: Abu Bakr asked for proof before he answered
he asked only whether the Prophet had said it, then said: if he said it, it is true.
the story says some believers turned back that morning
Ibn Ishaq reports that some who had believed turned away.
Abu Bakr's trust rested on knowing the speaker
he believed news from heaven came to him, so why not this?

games.q: you're Abu Bakr. a laughing crowd tells you your friend claims he went to Jerusalem and back in one night. what do you say?
games.why: he asked one question, did he say that, and then answered: if he said it, it is true.

practice: Bring to mind one person whose word has held, again and again: someone who said they'd come, and came, who told you the hard thing when the easy thing was right there.
Let their face settle in front of you, and notice how much of your life rests, quietly, on people like this. If you pray, you can thank God for that person by name.

wordCard.voice: Al-Siddiq, the one who affirms the truth. Abu Bakr's title, earned when he trusted the Prophet's word about the night journey without arguing the distance. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the one who affirms the truth; Abu Bakr's title.

carryVoice: Your line: he weighed the speaker, not the distance. Trust like that is built long before it's needed. See you tomorrow.
